title: [bug] Tauri v2.0.0-beta failed to build on Windows
body:
### Describe the bug

I recently migrated to v2, but encountered some issues. I am not sure if this issue should be raised here, but I think it may be related.
When I use github actions, it fails to build on Windows.
This may be related to my use of caching, as when I delete the cache, it can be successfully built.
But why?
This is a bit strange because there was no such issue in v1.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/reporter/tauri-windows-build

https://github.com/reporter/tauri-windows-build/actions/runs/8108131093/job/22160785334

### Expected behavior

It should be built successfully on Windows like v1.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: can you try removing `tauri-plugin-shell` from `Cargo.toml` and try again?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I have no idea why this is not working, cloning the same repo and building it on my machine works just fine.

Here is a couple of things to try:
1. remove the use of cache in CI just to rule out that it is not a cache issue
2. try building without tauri-action and use `pnpm tauri build -t <target>` instead
3. if that doesn't work try without `-t` flag

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I guess I was having the same issue, with `yarn`. 

```console

Compiling testeapp v0.1.0 (D:\a\tauri-ci-test\tauri-ci-test\apps\my_tauri_app\src-tauri)
error: failed to run custom build command for `testeapp v0.1.0 (D:\a\tauri-ci-test\tauri-ci-test\apps\my_tauri_app\src-tauri)`

Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `D:\a\tauri-ci-test\tauri-ci-test\apps\my_tauri_app\src-tauri\target\release\build\testeapp-e05d03921a11ecee\build-script-build` (exit code: 1)
  --- stdout
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=TAURI_CONFIG
  cargo:rerun-if-changed=tauri.conf.json
  cargo:rustc-cfg=desktop
  cargo:rustc-env=TAURI_ANDROID_PACKAGE_PREFIX=com_teste
  failed to read plugin permissions: failed to read file: The system cannot find the file specified. (os error 2)
warning: build failed, waiting for other jobs to finish...
       Error failed to build app: failed to build app
Error: Command failed with exit code 1: yarn tauri build

```
Building locally works, no cache involved.
Without cache, it builds.
With tauri-action `args: -v -d` also builds but doesn't solve the issue. 
With tauri-action `args: -t x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` it builds and solved for me as I'm targeting only Windows. Thanks for it @participant1, while you suggested to do it without tauri-action, I utilized the action anyway.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Using the target flag is basically the same as a cache reset because the flag changes the target dir.

So the question (I raised on discord iirc?) whether a single reset is enough or if it comes back, remains. So far I've not heard from it reappearing so I assume it's just an incompatibility with files from prior beta versions maybe?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I've tried multiple times by cleaning the cache to be sure the issue was the caching. The way it was build with the `-t` flag it did hit cache, building time dropped 3min (not great imo). The cache hit was from a successful build without the flag. 

Lastly, I did not upgraded to v2, the project was born v2. So maybe a different issue?

Note: the project is Windows only.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
The only part of the cache that could apply here is the global .cargo dir that holds the downloaded crates but 3 minutes is a bit much.
The -t flag changes the target dir from `target/release/` to `target/<target-flag>/release/` so nothing of the prior stuff should be re-used.

> Lastly, I did not upgraded to v2, the project was born v2. So maybe a different issue?

I was mainly thinking about the alpha to beta (or beta to beta) changes like the new ACL stuff since it talks about plugin permissions that were introduced in beta.

----

So if you're saying that without the -t flag it fails reliably even after clearing the cache then maybe something in tauri resolves the paths incorrectly without the -t flag? Weird that so far it only happened in CI though

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
>So if you're saying that without the -t flag it fails reliably even after clearing the cache 

Yeah, but don't take this as a scientific testing, I've done many tests that I lost track. But I'm more than 80% sure, if I could gauge

The only thing that worked so far was the -t flag with "cache-all-crates: true" (just tried without it and didn't worked). Cache action is "swatinem/rust-cache@v2"

The build step doesn't download anything, it goes to compiling. Not sure how this would behave in a ideal scenario.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
We're running into this issue too. It doesn't occur on macOS (the other platform we build for), but only occurs on Windows. Also it's stochastic, and has definitely sent us on some false paths due to occasionally building, but not always building.

Our initial tests are not consistent with it being a caching issue: we've seen it succeed multiple times with tweaks that shouldn't change the Rust cache. 

The characteristic error message we get is:

> failed to read plugin permissions: failed to read file: The system cannot find the file specified. (os error 2)
> warning: build failed, waiting for other jobs to finish...
>       Error failed to build app: failed to build app

I'm trying out `-t x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` as recommended, and will test it ~3 or so times and let you know what I find.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I'm back with results, tested `-t x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` as recommended, and I've seen no issues in 7 re-runs of the build, without any changes to caching.

Looks like adding a target somehow makes a difference?

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
still not resolved?
how to resolve this issue?

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
> I'm back with results, tested `-t x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` as recommended, and I've seen no issues in 7 re-runs of the build, without any changes to caching.
> 
> Looks like adding a target somehow makes a difference?

Unfortunately running into the same error despite defining an explicit target. [Ref to failed GA run](https://github.com/glzr-io/zebar/actions/runs/8221612715/job/22482170240?pr=36)

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Alright yeah, we also just ran into our first CI error despite an explicit target.

We've temporarily merged a change that disables our cache on Windows. That makes the build green again, but again, since it's flaky, it's hard to tell. I'll check back in if that breaks too. 

FWIW: This kinda sucks since it takes build times from 6 minutes to 19 minutes.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body: For me, what fixed it was deleting the `scr-tauri/target/debug/build` folder and then running `npm run tauri dev` again. Once I did that I also noticed that my antivirus put some of the files in quarantine, so I had to put that folder on the whitelist.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body: is this error maybe an issue of softlinks? How does tauri read the permissions file in windows

comments.author: participant9
comments.body: Same using `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, I solved it by clearing the cache

comments.body: Same, fixed by deleting all cache from `https://github.com/<User>/<Repo>/actions/caches`
